permutation_control.what_was_tested: SemIf/JEV-CPU's letter-choice logit readout (TheoLeeCJ/SemIf, 1770 stars) applied to THIS project's fine-tuned checkpoint, holding weights fixed and changing only the readout.
permutation_control.conclusion: The apparent confidence gain is a letter-A preference bias: the model answers 'A' regardless of what A denotes, so the probabilities carry no decision content. The naive readout does NOT fix the abstention on this checkpoint.
permutation_control.why: SemIf/JEV-CPU apply this readout to a BASE instruct model, whose next-token distribution over letters reflects the prompt. This checkpoint's backbone was fine-tuned with task-fitted heads, so its letter slots no longer carry the criteria.
permutation_control.correct_follow_up: Re-run the same readout on the BASE Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B that SemIf/JEV-CPU actually use, which is the only configuration in which the method is claimed to work.
permutation_control.limit: one checkpoint, 13 questions; the permutation control is the load-bearing part
